text.p: Mexican television company Grupo Televisa said on Wednesday it plans to cut costs by $270 million over the next three years and reduce its current total debt level of $988 million by $100 million, the company said in a statement.

"Through a combination of the strengthening Mexican economy, cost cutting measures and efforts to increase revenues, the Company expects its cash flow margins to exceed 25%," company CEO Guillermo Canedo White said.
Televisa is scheduled to meet with shareholders and analysts in New York Wednesday to outline the company's strategy and vision after patriarch Emilio Azcarraga Milmo's recent death.

The company said it plans to "freeze certain executive salaries and reduce overtime salaries." A new, performance based compensation policy of issuing stock options and other executive benefits in place of salary increases.
In addition, the company is looking to cut real estate rental expenses and promotional expenses for records and publishing, it said.

"The Company will incur estimated one-time restructuring charges of approximately $80 million, most of which relate to severance and termination charges of senior executives and their staffs," the statement said. Televisa added that it expected aggregate interest expenses of $135-$145 million compared with $245 million in 1996.
